settings.title: Basic hand tools
settings.description: A hacksaw, files, sandpaper, a measuring tape — no power tools. Everything else is in the kit.

settings.title: A bit of space
settings.description: A sturdy table around 1200 × 600 mm and a spot the frame can sit undisturbed while joints cure.

settings.title: A few weekends
settings.description: 25–35 hours across multiple sessions. No rush — bamboo is forgiving and most mistakes are fixable.

settings.title: Set the geometry
settings.description: Lock upright city geometry on the jig — comfortable, with mounts for racks, mudguards and lights.

settings.title: Join & wrap
settings.description: Bond the tubes with epoxy and wrap each joint with carbon-fibre tow.

settings.title: Cure
settings.description: Leave it for a full cure — that's where maximum joint strength comes from.

settings.title: Sand, seal & ride
settings.description: Sand smooth, seal the bamboo, fit the headset and bottom bracket. Adventure awaits.

settings.quote: It rides great and it's so comfortable — the only problem is everyone who sees it wants to talk about it or have a go.
To see the bike the first time and sit on it was euphoria. I was more taken than when I got my new car (sorry, car).

settings.question: Can I really ride it in the rain every day?
settings.answer: Yes. Finished frames are sealed with a weatherproof epoxy lacquer. Dry your bike after wet rides and store it indoors, and it'll give you years of riding — many of our earliest builds are still ridden daily.

settings.question: How much maintenance does a bamboo commuter need?
settings.answer: Very little. Build it single-speed and there's almost nothing to service — no derailleur to adjust. Keep the chain clean, dry the frame after wet rides, and inspect the joints once a year. That's it.

settings.question: Will it handle hills and city traffic?
settings.answer: The frame is single-speed or hub-gear ready, so you can spec gearing to suit your route and hills. The upright geometry gives you excellent visibility in traffic, and it fits standard racks, mudguards and lights.

settings.question: Is it strong and secure enough for daily city use?
settings.answer: Very strong for its weight. Bamboo is a light, hollow natural composite and every joint is reinforced with carbon-fibre, giving a high strength-to-weight ratio. Our bamboo is independently tested at Swansea University. Builders ride these frames daily and tour continents — with proper care they last for years.

settings.question: Can I get it through Cycle to Work?
settings.answer: Yes. Frame kits from £375 are eligible for standard Cycle to Work schemes — UK employees typically save 25–39% through salary sacrifice. We accept Cyclescheme, Cycle Solutions, Evans and Halfords.
